states.name: Oregon
states.permitNotice: Oregon generally requires a Waterway Access Permit for non-motorized boats. Exemptions apply on some trips, so check the current Marine Board rules.

states.name: Washington
states.permitNotice: Washington generally requires a Discover Pass to park at state-managed launches (WDFW, State Parks and DNR); a WDFW Vehicle Access Pass covers WDFW sites only. Federal, county, city and utility launches set their own fees.

states.name: Utah
states.permitNotice: Many Utah river trips need a federal permit: Dinosaur NM (NPS), Desolation/Gray Canyons, Westwater Canyon, the San Juan and Labyrinth Canyon (BLM) and Canyonlands (NPS). Most permits are booked on Recreation.gov. Some launches charge fees. Check the managing agency before you go.

states.name: Arizona
states.permitNotice: Several Arizona river trips need a permit. The Grand Canyon (Lees Ferry or Diamond Creek) needs a National Park Service river permit, and the Hualapai Tribe charges fees to use Diamond Creek. The Upper Salt (Mar 1 to May 15) needs a Tonto National Forest permit plus a White Mountain Apache permit. Lower Salt and Verde sites on the Tonto may need a Tonto Pass. Many permits are booked on Recreation.gov. Check the managing agency before you go.

states.name: Colorado
states.permitNotice: Some Colorado river trips need a permit or pass: Dinosaur NM (NPS; including a one-day play permit to take out at Deerlodge after floating from upstream), Gunnison Gorge Wilderness and Ruby-Horsethief overnight camping (BLM), self-issued DENCA overnight permits, and CPW State Parks passes (including Arkansas Headwaters fee sites). Some launches charge fees. Check the managing agency before you go.

rivers.name: Boise River (Greenbelt)
rivers.gaugeName: Boise River at Glenwood Bridge nr Boise
rivers.blurb: Idaho's busiest tube run — Barber Park to downtown, with a city shuttle and 100,000+ floaters a summer.

sections.notes: The classic Boise float. About 2–3 hours in a tube. Glass is banned. Ada County shuttle in season.
Quieter miles west of downtown. Watch for diversion structures and the south channel split.

rivers.name: Clearwater River
rivers.blurb: Big, warm, summer water from Orofino toward Lewiston. A North Idaho alternative to the crowded Greenbelt.

sections.notes: Wide river, easy current. Jet boats and fishing traffic on weekends.
Longer valley miles into the Lewiston area. Wind can come up the canyon in the afternoon.

rivers.name: Henry's Fork (Ashton)
rivers.blurb: Below Mesa Falls — Warm River and Ashton water, slower than the Box and still packed with rainbows.

sections.notes: Put in below Mesa Falls. Do not launch above the falls. Gentle gradient, watch for diversion dams near Ashton.
Valley miles toward the Snake confluence. Irrigation can skinny this stretch in late summer.

rivers.name: Henry's Fork (Box Canyon)
rivers.blurb: Island Park Dam to Last Chance — a short basalt canyon on some of the most famous trout water in the West.

sections.notes: Cold, rocky, and crowded with anglers. Give waders room. Harriman State Park below Last Chance is mostly closed to boats — don't float into the Ranch.

rivers.name: Lochsa River
rivers.blurb: Highway 12 whitewater. A spring Class III–IV that is over by the time the rest of Idaho is just warming up.

sections.notes: Peak is May–June. Not a tube float. USGS stage at this gauge is not the Lowell Bridge staff — check Lochsa.info for the boater gauge.
Packed rapids to the Selway confluence. Miss the takeout and you are on the Clearwater.

rivers.name: North Fork Payette (Cabarton)
rivers.blurb: Idaho's hardest roadside creek. Cabarton to Banks is continuous Class IV–V — experts only.

sections.notes: Not a float trip. Steep, wooded, and famous for wrapping boats. Experienced whitewater crews only — or watch from the highway.

rivers.name: Payette River (Banks)
rivers.blurb: Idaho's closest commercial whitewater to Boise. Banks to Horseshoe Bend — waves, holes, and a highway shuttle.

sections.notes: Upper Main. Payette River Pass parking. Not a tube float. Bennett's Rock is the first real drop.
Mixmaster and the rest of the Lower Main. Rafts and kayaks. Scout or go with a guide if it's new water.

rivers.name: Salmon River (Riggins)
rivers.blurb: Lower Salmon country. Day floats past Riggins, or the multi-day Hammer Creek to Heller Bar desert canyon.

sections.notes: Town-to-town. Warm water in summer, jet boats possible. Time Zone Rapid is the named drop.
The Lower Salmon. Typically 3–4 days. Snowhole is the big rapid. BLM camps, rattlesnakes, and a serious shuttle.

rivers.name: Salmon River (Salmon)
rivers.blurb: The River of No Return at town scale — Salmon to North Fork is a big, friendly Class I–II day.

sections.notes: Highway 93 shuttle. Big water, easy gradient. North Fork is where the Middle Fork comes in and the wilderness section begins.

rivers.name: Selway River (Permit)
rivers.blurb: Idaho's other permit-lottery classic. 47 canyon miles, one launch a day, no cell service.

sections.notes: Forest Service permit required. Typically 4–5 days in May–July. Moose Creek is midway. Portage or scout Selway Falls at the end.

rivers.name: South Fork Payette
rivers.gaugeName: South Fork Payette River at Lowman
rivers.blurb: Canyon water out of Lowman — hot springs on the bank, Swirly Canyon in the middle, Garden Valley at the bottom.

sections.notes: Warm up. Staircase above Lowman is a separate Class IV run — don't put in there by mistake.
Swirly Canyon miles. Payette River Pass sites. Take out before you join the Main at Banks if that's the plan.

rivers.name: South Fork Snake (Canyon)
rivers.blurb: The Conant canyon — largest remaining Yellowstone-cutthroat fishery, and no takeout in the middle.

sections.notes: Full-day canyon. No intermediate ramp. Cottonwood gallery, eagles, and a committed float.
River opens into the Heise valley. Twin Bridges is an optional pullout. Watch irrigation diversions.

rivers.name: South Fork Snake (Swan Valley)
rivers.blurb: Palisades Dam to Conant — big cutthroat water in Swan Valley before the canyon walls close in.

sections.notes: Dam-controlled. Fall Creek falls comes in river-left. Palisades Creek is an optional early takeout.

rivers.name: Deschutes River (Maupin)
rivers.blurb: Oregon's most-run whitewater day trip. Dam-fed, warm, and steady all summer through the canyon at Maupin.

sections.notes: Wapinitia and Boxcar are the big ones. A Deschutes boater pass is required for every person.
Oak Springs is the rapid to scout. Sandy Beach is the LAST take-out — Sherars Falls below is not runnable.

rivers.name: Grande Ronde River
rivers.blurb: Remote northeast Oregon canyon trip with easy water — a good first multi-day float.

sections.notes: Usually 2–3 days. A free self-issued river permit is required. The Wenaha River comes in at Troy. Few roads, so plan your shuttle ahead.

rivers.name: John Day River (Clarno)
rivers.gaugeName: John Day River at Service Creek
rivers.blurb: Undammed desert canyon float. Spring flows only — by late summer it's too low to boat.

sections.notes: A Recreation.gov boating permit is required year-round between Service Creek and Tumwater Falls. Clarno Rapid near the start is the hardest drop — scout it. The gauge is at Service Creek, just upstream.

rivers.name: McKenzie River
rivers.blurb: Clear, cold, and quick — the river the McKenzie drift boat was built for, east of Eugene.

sections.notes: Fast, continuous and cold even in August. Take out at Ben and Kay Dorris to avoid Marten Rapid immediately downstream.

rivers.name: Owyhee River (Lower)
rivers.blurb: Spring-only desert canyon in Oregon's far southeast corner. Hot springs, big walls, and a short boating window.

sections.notes: Usually floatable only March–May. A free BLM self-issue river permit is required. Scout Montgomery Rapid. Birch Creek is four-wheel-drive access; the road may close when soils are saturated.

rivers.name: Rogue River (Grants Pass)
rivers.blurb: Hellgate Canyon day floats below Grants Pass — the easy half of the Rogue, with jet boats for company.

sections.notes: Floats through Hellgate Canyon. Watch for jet boats and give them room in narrow spots.

rivers.name: Rogue River (Wild & Scenic)
rivers.blurb: The classic Oregon multi-day: Grave Creek to Foster Bar through roadless canyon, with lodges along the way.

sections.notes: BLM permit lottery in the main season. Most boats line or run the fish ladder at Rainie Falls. Scout Blossom Bar — it is the serious one.

sections.notes: Easy current through the canyon. BLM charges a $5 day-use fee ($15 overnight) at its Yakima River Canyon recreation sites, which are open year-round (https://www.blm.gov/visit/yakima-river-canyon-campgrounds).
